syllabus_topics: Development, compilation and debugging of a program
Notion of lexicon, syntax and semantics
Selection, repetition and flow control instructions
Scope and lifetime of a variable
Modularity and structuring: division by files
Notions of complexity and sorting algorithms

assessment_methods.method: Project Component (1 project with two deliveries and oral discussion)

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 40% (maximum of MAPs average or exam) + 20% (average of labs 2, 3, 5 and 6) + 40% (project grade after oral discussion). A final grade of at least 9.5 values is required. The exam or MAPs average must be at least 8 values, and the project grade (after oral discussion) must also be at least 8 values. An oral project discussion is mandatory if the project grade exceeds 17 values, or at the laboratory teacher's discretion to differentiate group members' grades or validate work. Projects are checked for plagiarism, and highly probable copies (>= 90%) result in project annulment.
bibliography: Brian W. Kernighan, Dennis M. Ritchie, The C Programming Language - The ANSI edition, Prentice-Hall, 1988 (main)

John Guttag, Introduction to Computation and Programming Using Python: With Application to Understanding Data, MIT Press, Second Edition, 2016 (main)
